title: CRM Graveyard
sub: A LinkedIn series about the problems that pile up inside a CRM, with a different visual idea for every post.
description: CRM Graveyard: a LinkedIn series for B2Ne about the problems that pile up inside a CRM. Fourteen posts and two videos, each with its own visual grammar, tracked in a ledger. By Riya Dutta.
facts: Founders and sales leads at small and mid-sized B2B tech companies
Everything, end to end: concept, copy, design, video, posting and reading the results. I run B2Ne’s LinkedIn campaigns on my own.

hero.alt: The Close Date post: a staircase of struck-through close dates.

sections.title: One world, many visual grammars.
sections.lead: Every post lives in one B2Ne world (palette, type, the real logo, the same corners for kicker, logo and URL), but no two posts look alike.
sections.close: A ledger records each post’s problem and its visual grammar, so a new post is never a re-skin of an old one.

sections.title: Sixteen pieces, one ledger.

items.title: Graveyard (bonus)
items.text:
The problem: Leads contacted once, then abandoned.
The insight: Every CRM holds records that were started and never finished.

items.title: HubSpot Confessions

The problem: Deals stuck in an early stage for months.
The insight: Stage names hide stagnation.

items.title: The HubSpot Ouija Board

The problem: Nobody can explain where the pipeline went.
The insight: The CRM can't answer the question it exists for.

items.title: CRM Performance Review

The problem: Poor data hygiene, routing and adoption.
The insight: The CRM is judged like an employee who is failing.

The insight: The official label and the reality diverge.

items.title: Choose Your Own CRM Adventure

The insight: Most routing options are dead ends.

items.title: Speed to Lead
items.text:
The problem: Slow follow-up on new leads.
The insight: Waiting loses the lead to someone faster.

items.title: Good Month, Dead Month
items.text:
The problem: Results swing and nothing records why.
The insight: The CRM records outcomes, not causes.

items.title: Pipeline Alerts
items.text:
The problem: Notifications ignored until deals die.
The insight: Alert volume trains people to ignore alerts.

items.title: The List Nobody Touches
items.text:
The problem: Zombie lists nobody dares delete.
The insight: Fear of deleting keeps dead data alive.

items.title: The Sync Error
items.text:
The problem: The CRM and the spreadsheet disagree.
The insight: Two sources of truth means no truth.

items.title: The Handover
items.text:
The problem: Context trapped in one person; the CRM keeps the activity, not the knowledge.
The insight: A handover quietly becomes a reset.

items.title: The Close Date
items.when: Onion-skin typography (motion trail of a single field)
items.text:
The problem: The expected close date pushed forward every month.
The insight: A date that only moves one way is a habit, not a forecast.

A close date is supposed to describe the buyer's timeline.
Often it describes the seller's hope.
When the date passes, moving it forward a month is easier than asking what actually changed. So the deal never looks lost. It just looks late, again.
The forecast inherits that optimism. The pipeline review talks about the date instead of the deal.
Somewhere in that edit history is the real signal: a buyer whose priorities moved while the record stayed polite.
A date that only ever moves in one direction isn't a forecast. It's a habit.

sections.title: Counting what’s been used.
sections.note: Each backlog idea is paired with the problem it would fit, never used for its own sake: a record decaying character by character for stale data, a path that simply stops for ownership nobody holds.

sections.title: What the ledger stopped the series repeating.
sections.intro: After fifteen posts, the ledger named the patterns that had been used enough.

items.d: Six posts already used a centred headline, a small symbol and a punchline.
Four posts used an outlined interface card or form. Don’t add another.
Coral had been the “bad” signal in seven posts, but the brand palette has no coral. From post 14 on, the series stays within Navy, Indigo, Soft Blue and Ice.
A bell, a clock and a planchette carried three posts. Later posts let the composition do the work.

sections.title: The post that got deleted.
paras: One post tried AI-rendered glossy variants: glass panels, glow, real third-party logos and a distorted B2Ne logo. It was deleted on 1 Oct 2026 as off-brand.
It stays in the ledger as a record of what not to do.

sections.text: The first twelve posts were made in a design tool. From post 14, each post is an HTML source with a spec file beside it, rendered to 1080 × 1350 by a script.
